# pr-2338: gh-2336 [daily-publish] stale release drafts swept

## Description

Closes #2336
### Root Cause
The daily draft sweeper kept re-filing "stale release drafts swept" (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236) because every machine-loop leg leaves a per-ticket **artefact-cache draft release** `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` in the repo — the dmtools-agents factory writes each fa leg's session/output snapshots into it (`github_get_or_create_draft_release`, tag template `ai-{ticketKey}`, authored by ai-teammate, marker-less, no owning run). The sweeper had no lifecycle for that class: it swept the drafts only after 24h **and counted them as sweep findings**, so normal machine-loop traffic perpetually re-opened the issue with a wrong diagnosis ("a `gh release create` step died…" — nothing died; these caches are never meant to publish).

### Fix
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: new `artifacts` bucket for machine-account drafts whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` with a real lifecycle —
  - ticket entity `closed` (issues REST API; covers merged PRs) → **reclaimed immediately, any age** (a closed cycle never resumes; the pack's restore is non-fatal and recreates the cache on first run);
  - ticket still open, draft >24h → existing 24h backstop sweep (parked leg);
  - fresh + open → kept (an in-flight leg may be writing snapshots);
  - ticket-state lookup failure → fail-safe keep (never delete blind);
  - the class is excluded from the issue-filing counters, so the recurring sweep issue finally auto-closes when only cache traffic remains; E1 holds for human-authored `ai-*` drafts, and machine-authored `vX.Y.Z` drafts stay bot-bucket findings.
- `docs/ci.md` + `daily-publish.yml` sweep-job comment: document the artefact-cache lifecycle.

### Test Coverage
- `test/release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart` — 9 new tests (TDD, written first, RED before the fix): cycle-end reclaim (fresh `ai-gh-*` + `ai-pr-*`), sweep-issue auto-close on cache-only traffic, keep-when-open, 24h backstop for open/unknown state, fail-safe keep on lookup failure, E1 for human `ai-*`, machine `vX.Y.Z` stays a finding, mixed-traffic issue separation — all PASS.
- Regression: `release_hygiene_test.dart` + `release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart` + `release_flow_race_test.dart` — 134 tests PASS (gh-2287/gh-2318/gh-2105 semantics preserved).

### Notes
- Sweep-token impact: one extra `GET repos/<repo>/issues/<n>` per cache draft (~5–10/day) — covered by the job's existing `issues: write` grant.
- Cache-loss window is unchanged in practice: closed tickets could already have their cache swept at 24h; a reopened ticket now starts with a fresh session (the restore path is contractually non-fatal).
- The recurring sweep issue this ticket auto-files will close itself on the first post-merge clean sweep.

## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.

# pr-2338: gh-2336 [daily-publish] stale release drafts swept

## Description

Closes #2336
### Root Cause
The daily draft sweeper kept re-filing "stale release drafts swept" (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236) because every machine-loop leg leaves a per-ticket **artefact-cache draft release** `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` in the repo — the dmtools-agents factory writes each fa leg's session/output snapshots into it (`github_get_or_create_draft_release`, tag template `ai-{ticketKey}`, authored by ai-teammate, marker-less, no owning run). The sweeper had no lifecycle for that class: it swept the drafts only after 24h **and counted them as sweep findings**, so normal machine-loop traffic perpetually re-opened the issue with a wrong diagnosis ("a `gh release create` step died…" — nothing died; these caches are never meant to publish).

### Fix
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: new `artifacts` bucket for machine-account drafts whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` with a real lifecycle —
  - ticket entity `closed` (issues REST API; covers merged PRs) → **reclaimed immediately, any age** (a closed cycle never resumes; the pack's restore is non-fatal and recreates the cache on first run);
  - ticket still open, draft >24h → existing 24h backstop sweep (parked leg);
  - fresh + open → kept (an in-flight leg may be writing snapshots);
  - ticket-state lookup failure → fail-safe keep (never delete blind);
  - the class is excluded from the issue-filing counters, so the recurring sweep issue finally auto-closes when only cache traffic remains; E1 holds for human-authored `ai-*` drafts, and machine-authored `vX.Y.Z` drafts stay bot-bucket findings.
- `docs/ci.md` + `daily-publish.yml` sweep-job comment: document the artefact-cache lifecycle.

### Test Coverage
- `test/release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart` — 9 new tests (TDD, written first, RED before the fix): cycle-end reclaim (fresh `ai-gh-*` + `ai-pr-*`), sweep-issue auto-close on cache-only traffic, keep-when-open, 24h backstop for open/unknown state, fail-safe keep on lookup failure, E1 for human `ai-*`, machine `vX.Y.Z` stays a finding, mixed-traffic issue separation — all PASS.
- Regression: `release_hygiene_test.dart` + `release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart` + `release_flow_race_test.dart` — 134 tests PASS (gh-2287/gh-2318/gh-2105 semantics preserved).

### Notes
- Sweep-token impact: one extra `GET repos/<repo>/issues/<n>` per cache draft (~5–10/day) — covered by the job's existing `issues: write` grant.
- Cache-loss window is unchanged in practice: closed tickets could already have their cache swept at 24h; a reopened ticket now starts with a fresh session (the restore path is contractually non-fatal).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, the repo's machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE,
#     default ai-teammate — gh-2287: its drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are
#     User-typed and marker-less but machine-created), OR the body
#     carries a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>`
#     marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them. EXCEPTION (gh-2318): a fresh draft with a
#     well-formed release-draft-owner marker is RECLAIMED immediately when
#     its owner run completed, no ci.yml push train on the tag is still
#     queued/in-flight, and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train
#     failed with release-provenance SKIPPED (the publish point is
#     unreachable — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs, so
#     nobody will ever publish it; the same criterion as ci.yml's gh-2230
#     train-draft-guard, which only sees drafts visible at train end).
#     A rerunnable (FAILED) provenance keeps the draft as the rerun
#     --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899) until it goes stale below;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# ── artefact-cache drafts have their own lifecycle (gh-236) ────────────────
# The machine loop (dmtools-agents factory: timerAutoCommitAndSave.js →
# releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile → github_get_or_create_draft_release, tag
# template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots
# as assets of a per-ticket DRAFT release `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>`, created
# with the ai-teammate token — User-typed, marker-less, no Actions run owns
# it. Those drafts are caches by design (never published, assets
# best-effort), NOT failed release-train drafts — but without a lifecycle
# they rotted 24h, were swept as generic bot-bucket findings, and re-filed
# the recurring sweep issue every day (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236). The
# guard: a machine-account draft whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is
#   - RECLAIMED NOW, any age, when the ticket entity is `closed` — a closed
#     cycle never resumes (a reopened ticket starts a fresh session; the
#     pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates the cache on "first
#     run"), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends;
#   - swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket is still open (a
#     parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes);
#   - kept untouched while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an
#     in-flight leg may be writing snapshots into it);
#   - KEPT on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only
#     the 24h backstop then applies.
# The class is EXCLUDED from the sweep-issue finding counters: reclaiming a
# lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, not a stale-draft finding, so
# the issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored
# `ai-*` drafts are NOT lifecycle-managed (E1 holds — they stay listed,
# kept), and machine-authored non-matching drafts (e.g. a machine-authored
# `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the bot bucket and remain findings.
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
# The repo's machine-account identity (same env + default as
# daily_publish_report.sh): drafts authored by it are pipeline-created —
# gh-2287: the ai-teammate factory's drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are User-typed
# and marker-less, so author-only Bot detection bucketed them as human and
# they rotted forever while the sweep issue never auto-closed.
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

# the tag ref — release-provenance is the sole publish point, gh-1801).

# "skipped" means the publish point is UNREACHABLE (`rerun --failed` never
# resurrects skipped jobs — the gh-2230 train-guard criterion), "failure"

# recovered). `in_flight` is "in_flight" when ANY fetched ci.yml push run
# on the tag has a null conclusion (queued or in progress), "none" when all
# have concluded, and "unknown" if that check fails; the fresh-draft reclaim

# publish even when an older train failed. The publish-point job is matched
# by its ci.yml `name:` —
# "Sign release checksums" (pinned by test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart,

# lookup failed; every consumer degrades fail-safe (keep), and nothing
# here may gate the stale >24h delete (the diagnosis is never a
# precondition — gh-2105).
train_diagnosis() {
  local tag="$1" train_json failed_train train_id jobs_json in_flight
  train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
    --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
  in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -r '
    if any(.[]; .conclusion == null) then "in_flight" else "none" end
  ' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
    ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
      | if . == null then empty else
          {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
        end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  [ -n "$failed_train" ] || return 0
  train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  jobs_json=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s' \
    "$train_id" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '([.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums")][0].conclusion // "")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$in_flight"
}

  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:

#                    -> lifecycle-managed: reclaim at cycle end / 24h
#                    backstop / keep in flight; NEVER a sweep finding

#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list

#                    reclaim: a marked draft whose owner run completed and
#                    whose tag's train failed with release-provenance
#                    SKIPPED (publish point unreachable) is deleted NOW

  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { stale: ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage),
        bucket: (
          # gh-236 first: the machine loop artefact-cache class, keyed on
          # the machine account AND the `ai-{ticketKey}` tag shape the
          # factory releaseArtefacts.buildTag() produces (lowercased,
          # non-alnum to '-', so `GH-2288` becomes `ai-gh-2288`,
          # `pr-2293` becomes `ai-pr-2293`). Human-authored ai-* drafts and
          # machine-authored vX.Y.Z drafts never match and fall through to
          # the buckets below.
          if (((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
              and ((.tag_name // "") | test("^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$")))
          then "artifacts"
          elif ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.

                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]

deleted_count=0

reclaimed_count=0

fresh_count=0
# gh-236: machine-loop artefact-cache drafts — lifecycle-managed, NOT

#   reclaimed at cycle end (ticket closed, any age) / swept by the 24h

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.

[125 more lines in file. Use offset=61 to continue.]

- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: docs/ci.md contradicts the implemented lookup-failure behavior**

`docs/ci.md:266` states the artefact-cache class is "kept on ANY ticket-state
lookup failure (never delete blind)". The implemented — and tested — behavior
is narrower: a lookup failure blocks only the **early** reclaim; a stale (>24h)
cache is still deleted by the 24h backstop:

```bash
# scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:241-245
elif [ "$stale" = "true" ]; then
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
```

Everything else in the PR states the carve-out; this sentence is the outlier:

- the script's own header (sweep_stale_drafts.sh:47-48): "KEPT on any
  ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — **only the 24h backstop
  then applies**";
- the PR description: "ticket-state lookup failure → fail-safe keep (never
  delete blind); only the 24h backstop then applies";
- the `art-backstop-unknown-stale` test, which asserts the DELETE fires and
  reasons "it only blocks the early reclaim".

An auditor tracing a deleted state-unknown cache would read docs/ci.md as a
promise of keep — and conclude the sweeper misbehaved, when in fact it did
exactly what the header/tests specify.

Two prose strings repeat the same misstatement by describing the swept cohort
as "ticket still open" when it also includes state-UNKNOWN drafts:

- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:244` — "swept after 24h with the ticket still
  open (parked leg …)" — fires for lookup failures too;
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:412` — "swept after 24h when the ticket stays
  open".

Fix (one lap, doc-only + two prose strings): reword docs/ci.md:266 to
"kept on any ticket-state lookup failure — only the 24h backstop then applies"
(mirroring the script header), and make both prose strings say "with the
ticket still open **or its state unknown**".

💡 **SUGGESTION: the gh stub's permission model doesn't cover the new issues lookup**

The stub maps every `api` call to `need=contents`
(`test/release_hygiene_test_support.dart:536` — pre-existing line), so the new
per-ticket cycle-state lookup `gh api "repos/$repo/issues/$num"`
(`scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:234`) passes permission enforcement in tests
even though in production it needs the `issues` scope. The PR Notes say the
call is "covered by the job's existing `issues: write` grant", and
docs/ci.md's stub rationale (review of #294) is explicitly "a dropped grant
fails CI instead of silently degrading" — but for **this** call a dropped
`issues:` grant stays green: the stub serves the fixture regardless of the
granted scopes, while production 403s every lookup, `state` stays empty, and
the early reclaim dies silently (the 24h backstop survives, so nothing breaks
loudly — the feature just stops working with no test signal).

Mirror the #294 precedent this stub comment cites — refine the need-case so
`api repos/*/issues/<n>` requires `issues`:

```bash
case "\$cmd \$2" in
  "run list"|"run view"|"run watch"|"run rerun") need=actions ;;
  "issue "*|"label "*) need=issues ;;
  "release "*) need=contents ;;
esac
# gh api: scope follows the resource path (gh-236 lookup = issues:read)
[ "\$cmd" = "api" ] && case "\$2" in
  */issues/*) need=issues ;;
  *) need=contents ;;
esac
```

Suggestion-level: the `issues` grant as a whole is still pinned indirectly —
the auto-close test (`issue close`) 403s without it — so nothing blocks merge
here; this just closes the residual silent-degradation window on the new call.
